The instant application, under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, has been filed on behalf of the applicant/petitioner seeking anticipatory bail in FIR bearing No. 46/2024 registered at Police Station - Cyber Police Station (South), Delhi for offences punishable under Section 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter "IPC").
2.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submitted that the applicant is an innocent person and has not committed any offence as alleged in the FIR.

3. It is submitted that the applicant's name is not mentioned in the present FIR, and his name was disclosed only by the accused i.e., Golu in his statement, wherein, he stated that he had handed over the bank account kit, in which the complainant transferred the amount, to the applicant herein.

It is further submitted that no transaction has ever happened between the applicant and the complainant, and the applicant's name has been roped in by the accused Golu only to falsely implicate the applicant because of enmity among them.

sentences.text: It is submitted that after the aforesaid disclosure, the applicant herein was served with the notice under Section 42A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter "CrPC").
It is also submitted that the applicant is ready to and willing to join the investigation.
6. It is further submitted that there is no history of previous involvement of the applicant in any criminal case and he has clean antecedents.
Moreover, the applicant undertakes to abide by all terms and conditions as imposed by this Court while granting anticipatory bail.
Therefore, in view of the foregoing submissions, it is prayed that the instant application may be allowed and the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

7. Per contra, learned APP appearing on behalf of the State vehemently opposed the instant anticipatory bail application submitting to the effect that the applicant is the master mind of the crime and he plays a significant role in the commission of the offence in the present FIR.
She has referred to the CDR record of the applicant herein stating to the effect that the applicant made 767 calls to the accused Golu within a period of 5 months.

8. It is submitted that the investigating agencies are trying to tackle the crime syndicate; therefore,
custodial interrogation of the applicant is required to unearth the actual facts and circumstances.
9.
Therefore, in view of the above facts and circumstance, it is prayed that the instant application may be rejected.

Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the contents made in the application as well as the status report filed by the State.
11. The applicant herein is charged with the offences punishable under Section 420 of the IPC.
Further, the allegation against the applicant is that he is the mastermind of the crime syndicate and that the CDR reveals that he has been in regular communication with the accused Golu.

12. However, it is pertinent to note here that the applicant herein has been implicated and was served with the notice under Section 41A of the CrPC only on the basis of the disclosure statement made by the accused Golu, and no other evidence has been produced before this Court to show the criminal conduct of the applicant which would clearly establish his role in the commission of the offence alleged in the FIR.
13.

Therefore, at this stage, taking into consideration the seriousness of the offence and the undertaking given by the applicant that he shall abide by all terms and conditions as imposed by this Court while granting anticipatory bail and that he will join the investigation as and when required,
this Court is inclined to grant interim anticipatory bail to the applicant.

a) he shall surrender his passport, if any, to the Investigating Officer and shall under no circumstances leave India without prior permission of the Court This is a digitally signed order.
